title: Chapter 10: Turtle-Style Trading Step by Step

claims.text: Compare systems on a common data universe, period and sizing policy, and disclose residual differences in exposure, costs and execution.
Signals from a completed close should execute only at a later available price, with gaps and costs accounted for.
Treat the chapter's six systems as distinct historical specifications rather than interchangeable descriptions of the original Turtle rules.
A simpler system or time exit can outperform a more complex alternative in a particular sample; this challenges universal complexity and exit claims but does not isolate all profit to entry.
Reject the implication that historical no-stop superiority establishes that stops are universally unnecessary. Loss capacity and gap exposure require independent limits.
Small extensions of the historical window can materially change ranking and maximum drawdown; lock evaluation horizons before seeing results.

assimilation: Specify a complete executable variant before testing. Historical rankings remain hypotheses. Retain portfolio constraints and compare costs, exposure and drawdown across predeclared periods, including periods when earlier winners fail.
adversarial_review: The 27 named markets differ from the earlier 28-market account. Chapter 5's 50/300 moving-average filter becomes 25/350 here. The ATR channel prose specifies +7/-3 ATR while figure 10-1 looks roughly symmetric; do not silently repair it. ATR lookback and several execution details remain unspecified. No-stop systems still have exits, and entry loss can contribute to drawdown despite page 133's categorical denial. A time exit still contributes to returns; its success cannot attribute all profitability to entry. The tables do not disclose costs, roll rules or survivorship controls sufficiently for replication. Historical Sharpe values inherit the earlier questionable definition. Table 10-3's 48.4% drawdown increase is approximately 50%, while unchanged rounded time-exit drawdown does not mean unchanged performance. The June-to-November extension is author-observed hindsight, not this project's holdout. Common sizing does not equal common risk. The chapter does not actually specify the promised simple price-lookback system. Reject the epigraph's assertion that simple methods beat complicated methods every time.
memory_delta: Freeze a fully specified system, not a book label. Preserve parameter inconsistencies. Historical no-stop results and changing rankings support sensitivity testing, not removal of risk controls or forecasts of replicated returns.
reading_provenance: Read all PDF pages 120-135 and inspected all six charts and three performance tables, including table 10-3 continued on page 135.
